title: DHS Proposes Rule to Overhaul EB-5 Investor Visa Program With Stronger Protections and Oversight
excerpt: The proposed regulation would codify sweeping reforms to the immigrant investor program, introducing new compliance standards for Regional Centers and critical safeguards for investors.
body:
The Department of Homeland Security has announced a proposed rule that could fundamentally reshape the EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program — one of the most popular pathways for high-net-worth Indian nationals seeking permanent residency in the United States.

## What the New Rule Would Change

The proposed regulation, formally titled "EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022; Ensuring the Integrity of the EB-5 Program," would implement key provisions of the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act (RIA) that Congress enacted in 2022. While USCIS has been applying many of these reforms through policy guidance, this rule would codify them into federal regulations for the first time.

According to immigration law firm Wolfsdorf Rosenthal LLP, the rule is expected to address several critical areas:

- **Regional Center oversight**: New standards for designation, suspension, and termination of Regional Centers, which pool investor capital for job-creating projects
- **Compliance obligations**: Detailed requirements for Regional Centers and their affiliated parties
- **Investor protections**: Safeguards for investors who comply with program requirements but may be affected by Regional Center misconduct beyond their control
- **Automatic petition revocation**: Clarity on when and how USCIS can revoke immigrant petitions, and the circumstances under which investors may retain eligibility

## Why This Matters for Indian Investors

India has consistently ranked among the top countries for EB-5 visa applications. The program requires a minimum investment of $800,000 in a Targeted Employment Area (or $1,050,000 elsewhere) that creates at least 10 full-time jobs for U.S. workers. For Indian nationals facing decades-long backlogs in employment-based green card categories like EB-2 and EB-3, the EB-5 program has offered a faster alternative path to permanent residency.

The proposed rule's investor protection provisions are particularly significant. Under the RIA, investors who have acted in good faith should be protected even if their Regional Center faces enforcement action. The new regulations would clarify exactly how these protections work in practice — providing much-needed certainty for investors who have committed substantial capital.

## What Happens Next

The proposed rule has not yet been published in the Federal Register. Once published, it will undergo a public comment period before any final regulation takes effect. Current EB-5 filings continue to be governed by existing law and USCIS policy guidance.

Immigration attorneys are encouraging Regional Centers, developers, and investors to participate in the public comment process once the rule is published, particularly on practical implementation issues and investor safeguards.

*Sources: Wolfsdorf Rosenthal LLP, DHS announcement*
author: Diaspora Desk
